Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $32 million class fund distributed automatically to identified members, plus $6 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Any fees not awarded would benefit the class. Brightline need not agree not to oppose the fee request. We are ready to discuss the overall economics, but automatic distribution is important given the records available.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your emphasis on automatic payments and agree that the available records support that approach. To narrow the overall economics, Brightline proposes a $29 million class fund plus $5 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval, with any unawarded fees going to the class and no clear-sailing commitment.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement to automatic distribution and to directing any unawarded fees to the class. To bridge the remaining gap, we propose a $31 million class fund and $5 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval, with the other terms unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your movement on the fund. Brightline can increase its offer to a $30 million class fund plus $5 million in fees and expenses, retaining automatic distribution and the other approval-conscious terms. This brings us close on overall economics.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $30 million class fund with automatic distribution, plus $5 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval, no clear-sailing commitment, and any unawarded fees going to the class.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial class recovery in light of the $64 million in disputed charges, litigation risk, and delay. Require automatic payments because Brightline can identify every member and charged card. Keep fees separate, subject to court approval, and direct any fee reduction to the class rather than Brightline.

The $38 million proposal is within authority and has strong approval prospects, but there is room to seek a lower total cash outlay without compromising automatic distribution or introducing fee provisions that could complicate approval.

The $29 million automatic-distribution fund is a strong offer given the $27.5 million trial-value estimate before certification risk. Its fee terms also cover the firm's investment. There is room to seek a modest improvement for the class without changing the protective distribution and fee provisions.

Their $36 million proposal is within authorization and has approval-friendly terms, but four rounds remain and a modest counteroffer may reduce Brightline’s total outlay without jeopardizing settlement.

The $30 million automatic class fund exceeds the $27.5 million undiscounted trial expected value, before certification, delay, and litigation risks. The $5 million fee remains subject to court approval, with any reduction benefiting the class. Accepting secures strong class relief without fee-related red flags.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: On behalf of the proposed class, Hargrove Lane LLP negotiated with Brightline after the complaint survived a motion to dismiss and before class certification. Our opening proposal was a $32 million class fund and $6 million in fees and expenses. Brightline countered with a $29 million fund and $5 million in fees and expenses. We then proposed a $31 million fund with $5 million in fees and expenses. Brightline offered a $30 million fund with $5 million in fees and expenses, which we accepted. Every proposal provided for automatic payments to identified class members, no clear-sailing commitment, and payment of any fees not awarded by the court to the class rather than Brightline. Fees were discussed alongside class relief from the first proposal; they were not deferred until after class relief was agreed. The $5 million fee remains subject to court approval.
